message.content: Lions mate during the breeding season (typically spring–summer). A male will approach a receptive female, often after a scent or vocal cue. He may display dominance through roaring, body posture, and scent marking. If the female accepts, they engage in copulation, which lasts only a few minutes but can occur repeatedly over several days. After mating, the male may guard the female from rivals, especially if he has recently taken over her pride. The female then carries the pregnancy for about 110 days before giving birth.
